jobs.occupation: Gen B Graduate Program, Water Treatment Engineer
jobs.description:
Start your future at one of Europe’s leading mining- and smelting companies and become part of Gen B! Begin a one-year journey designed to challenge and inspire you. As a graduate, you will gain in-depth, hands-on experience across different business areas, functions, and sites in Sweden, Finland, Norway, Portugal or Ireland, depending on your chosen position. 
 
To drive change for future generations, we need new ways of thinking, that’s why we encourage you to apply. You are the hearts behind tomorrow.  
 
A program designed for your future 
For one year, divided into three periods, you will explore how Boliden operates end to end, and how your own unique background and experience connect to the bigger picture. As a graduate, you are employed in a permanent position from day one and supported by an individual development program. Throughout the year several engaged and experienced colleagues, will guide you in your progress. You will become part of an international network of graduates and colleagues, expanding both your knowledge and connections. Six joint training weeks with top-class lecturers will challenge your thinking and give you the opportunity to further deepen your skills. After graduation you will continue your journey with a mentor for six months. In addition, you will receive practical training in project methodology and Boliden’s production methods, enabling you to apply what you learn directly in our operations. 
 
Learn more at Gen B - Boliden how you can step into a future where raw material meets your potential.  
 
Find your path 
As a graduate and part of Gen B, you will be given a unique gateway into Boliden. Whether you want to grow as an expert in business, engineering or tech, you will get the opportunity to grow in the area that excites you the most.  

In this role as a Water Treatment Engineer, you'll be part of a team working with water treatment in a mining and industrial environment. Depending on the final placement, you may work within an Environmental Department or a Concentrator/Processing Plant, combining process engineering and reporting with practical presence in the plant. 

Responsibilities: 
Support and develop water treatment processes in a mining and industrial environment 

Investigate process issues and identify practical, solution-focused improvements 

Combine engineering analysis and reporting with regular presence in the plant 

Build an understanding of equipment and how water treatment processes operate in practice 

Collaborate with operational employees, managers and specialists across different functions and sites 

Build internal networks and proactively identify colleagues who can contribute relevant expertise 

Prepare accurate and structured technical reports and communicate findings to different stakeholders 

Reporting in water quality and water consumption, as well as prepare accurate and structured technical reports and communicate findings to different stakeholders 

 
Qualifications: 
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Engineering with a clear connection to Process Engineering or Process Technology. A Master’s degree is strongly preferred. Courses in chemistry and environmental subjects are meritorious 

 
Who you are 
We think you are a forward thinker and a team thriver, who is naturally curious, and solutions oriented. You communicate with honesty and respect, are eager to take initiative and dedicated to follow through. Above all, you are ready to take responsibility and grow as an expert. 
 
What you bring 
You hold a relevant university degree completed in 2025 or later. You can communicate clearly in English, hold a valid driver’s license and are available to start in September 2027. 
 
This role may be based at Aitik or in the Boliden Area. The final location and organizational placement will be determined during the recruitment process, based on business needs. 
 
How to apply 
Submit your application and CV in English. The recruitment process includes assessments, interviews, and a final Assessment Center for selected candidates. 
The Assessment Center will take place in Stockholm, Sweden, on one day between February 16-19, 2027. Boliden will cover travel and accommodation expenses. Please ensure your availability between February 14-20, 2027, if you progress to the final stage. 

 About Boliden 
Boliden is at the forefront of advancing our industry through sustainable solutions and innovation. Every day, we work to reduce our footprint, and drive long-term progress. We are on a journey towards becoming the most sustainable and respected metal supplier in the world. With us, you will be part of a diverse workplace built on care, courage and responsibility. We work together to grow and take the lead. Our priority is your safety, well-being and growth. Make a lasting impact, in your everyday work, for future generations. Let a rock-solid career start with us. Learn more at boliden.com. 

Apply today to be part of something truly meaningful! 

Do you have any questions about your application? Please send an e-mail to genb@boliden.com.
Last day to apply for this position is November 17th 2026. Selection will be ongoing; we are looking forward to receiving your application as soon as possible 

Union information is available from Ingela Scherling, Saco +46 70 272 08 68, Andreas Mårtensson, Unionen, +46 70 541 83 93 or Peter Markström, Ledarna, +46 910 77 40 09.

Business Development Manager (Personal Care)
jobs.description:
Background: 
Melt&Marble harness precision fermentation to create the next generation of sustainable designer fats, tailored for applications ranging from delicious, climate-friendly foods to high-performance personal care products. 
We are growing our personal care commercial team and are looking for a Business Development Manager (personal care) to help turn early market traction into a growing business. Reporting to the Head of Business Development & Sales – Personal Care, you will combine hands-on business development with distributor and channel management, making sure brands, formulators, and our distribution partners have everything they need to adopt our ingredients successfully. 

Position Summary: 
The Business Development Manager will be a key day-to-day contact for Melt&Marble’s personal care customers and distribution partners. You will: 
Build and convert a pipeline of new business with personal care brands, contract manufacturers, and formulation houses. 
Manage and grow Melt&Marble’s relationships with personal care ingredient distributors, helping them sell our ingredients effectively in their markets. 
Coordinate samples, trials, and documentation between customers, distributors, and our R&D, regulatory, and operations teams. 

This is a hands-on, customer-facing role ideal for someone with experience in business development, account management, and distributor management in the personal care or cosmetic ingredients sector, who wants to grow with a fast-scaling company. While the focus is personal care, there is flexibility to contribute to our food business as priorities evolve. 
The role involves travel within Sweden and abroad and may require work outside normal office hours.

Key Responsibilities: 
Business development & pipeline management 
Identify, qualify, and develop new opportunities with personal care brands (from multinationals to innovative indie brands), contract manufacturers, and formulation houses, in line with the personal care commercial strategy. 
Own a defined portfolio of accounts and/or territories, managing opportunities from first contact through sampling, evaluation, and commercial agreement. 
Prepare proposals, quotations, and commercial documentation, support negotiations, and maintain accurate CRM records, pipeline forecasts, and sales reporting. 

Distributor & channel management 
Manage and grow relationships with distribution partners, including onboarding, training, joint account planning, business reviews, and performance tracking against agreed targets. 
Enable distributor sales and tech. teams with the necessary product knowledge, samples, technical and regulatory documentation, and marketing materials. 
Support the identification and onboarding of new distribution partners and coordinate forecasts, orders, and sample logistics with distributors and internal teams. 

Customer support & market insight 
Coordinate sample requests, formulation trials, and follow-ups with customers and distributors, working closely with R&D and application teams. 
Ensure customers and partners have timely access to product and regulatory documentation (e.g., TDS, SDS, INCI, REACH, natural origin index), in collaboration with the regulatory team. 
Collect and share customer feedback, market trends, and competitive intelligence to support product development, positioning, and commercial decisions.

Market presence & cross-functional collaboration 
Represent Melt&Marble at industry events, conferences, and trade shows, and support distributor-led customer events. 
Collaborate with marketing, R&D, regulatory, operations, and commercial teams to support sales initiatives, develop market-facing materials, and align business activities. 
As business needs evolve, contribute to business development activities across Melt&Marble's broader ingredient portfolio, leveraging commercial and channel-management expertise across sectors. 

 Requirements: 
A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in chemistry, cosmetic science, chemical engineering, life sciences, business, or a related field. 
Min. 4 years of experience in business development, sales, or account management in the personal care/cosmetic ingredients industry (supplier or distributor side). 
Hands-on experience managing distributor or channel partner relationships. 
Proven track record of building a pipeline and closing B2B deals, with strong CRM and pipeline discipline. 
Good understanding of the role of different ingredients in cosmetic formulations. 
Excellent communication skills in English.
Willingness to travel regularly.
Entrepreneurial mindset with ability to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced startup. 
Passion for sustainability and innovation in beauty. 

Bonus points: 
Experience working at, or closely with, a specialty ingredient distributor. 
Technical understanding of fats, oils, emollients, or other functional ingredients in formulations. 
Exposure to food ingredients, or experience selling ingredients across both food and personal care markets. 
Experience launching a novel or new-to-market ingredient. 
Familiarity with cosmetics regulatory requirements and documentation (e.g., EU Cosmetics Regulation, REACH, INCI listings, ISO 16128). 

We Offer: 
A mission-driven, collaborative environment where your work contributes to global sustainability and innovation in personal care. 
A high-growth startup culture that values initiative, creativity, & impact. 
The opportunity to help build Melt&Marble’s personal care business from an early stage, with a clear path for career development as it grows. 
Competitive remuneration, generous vacation package, and other benefits 

Location: Gothenburg, Sweden. 
Reports to: Head of Business Development & Sales – Personal Care 
How to apply: 
Applications should be in English and include:
Cover letter- tell us why you’re a great fit for Melt&Marble and this particular position (300 words max) 
CV outlining your experience, educational background and key skills, including contact info of 2 current/former supervisors and 1 colleague 

Application deadline: November 15th. Note! We evaluate applications as they are received, so please apply early.

For any questions, please email hr@meltmarble.com

jobs.occupation: PhD Student in Landscape Governance and Management
jobs.description:
Department of Landscape Architecture, Planning and Management
Third-cycle subject area:
Landscape architecture
Description of the doctoral project:
Governance and organisational alignment related to the operation and maintenance (O&M) of urban drainage infrastructures
Stormwater transports a wide range of pollutants from urban environments to receiving waters, posing major challenges for the protection of surface waters and coastal ecosystems. Urban drainage infrastructures, such as gully pots and stormwater ponds, play a critical role by retaining sediments and associated contaminants. However, their performance depends on effective operation and maintenance (O&M), which in practice is often reactive or based on fixed schedules, despite large spatial and temporal variability in sediment accumulation and vegetation development. This PhD project is part of a larger interdisciplinary research initiative aiming to enable a transition towards more data-driven and environmentally responsible maintenance of urban drainage infrastructures. The overall goal is to reduce pollutant loads to coastal and marine environments while supporting sustainable urban water management.
The PhD research will focus on identifying strategies for coherent long-term organisational set-ups and assess how stakeholder discourses, rules and resources shape the feasibility of different O&M schemes defined within the overall project. This includes assessment of governance feasibility of the various O&M schemes, and identification of alignment strategies, drawing on legal and policy frameworks and economic frameworks identified by partners in the overall project. The programmatic alignment theory, long-term strategic management, and elements of Nature-based Thinking (the organisational, ecological and social interdependencies) will be applied as basis for the analysis. Based on this, organisational and governance aspects of long-term urban drainage infrastructure maintenance will be described, as well as governance challenges and barriers for achieving healthy coastal environments will be identified.
Within this project, the PhD student will be involved in collaboration with stakeholders in both the water and wastewater industry and the green sector. The PhD student will communicate results both with the industry and international researchers.
About the position:
As a PhD student, you will perform both empirical and theoretical work. You will learn how to collect and analyse data within your research area as well as communicate your results at national and international conferences and in scientific journals. Most of your working time will be devoted to your own research studies, including both research and coursework. In addition, you will also carry out departmental duties, such as teaching and/or assisting in other research projects. You will have two or three supervisors who support you in your work.
Requirements:
To meet the general entry requirements you must have:
been awarded a second-cycle (Master's) qualification;
satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second-cycle, or
acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad (Higher Education Ordinance 1993:100, Chapter 7, Section 39).

The special entry requirements for the subject landscape architecture are the equivalent of at least 90 higher education credits in courses relevant to landscape architecture. At least 30 credits must be at second-cycle level. For applicants who do not fulfil these criteria, eligibility is verified on a case-by-case basis taking into account the research task.
You must also meet the equivalent English language requirements as those necessary for the Swedish upper-secondary qualification Engelska B/6.
Your profile:
Required qualifications:
A Master's degree (or equivalent) in natural resources engineering, civil engineering, landscape architecture/management, organisational/governance theory or a related field
Excellent communication skills in English, both written and spoken
Ability to work independently and take initiative
Ability to engage with new research areas

Desirable qualifications:
Good communication skills in Swedish or another Scandinavian language, both written and spoken
A valid car driver's licence recognized in Sweden

About us:
The Landscape Governance and Management research group has a strong position in research and education on urban landscape governance and management, including urban water systems, primarily stormwater. The group consists of about 15 members and the group's overall goal is to contribute to how governance and management can be developed to support the sustainability, use and relevance of outdoor environments, often within applied development and in innovation-driven contexts.

Form of employment / Funding:

jobs.occupation: Automotive Cybersecurity Engineer – Software-Defined Vehicles
jobs.description:
Vehicles are increasingly defined by software: centralised computing, over-the-air updates and connected services. That makes cybersecurity a core part of vehicle development. Cyber Instincts is building a network of automotive cybersecurity specialists to take on assignments with OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers in the Gothenburg region. If you work with product cybersecurity and want to help shape secure, software-defined vehicles, we’d like to hear from you.
What you could work on

Threat Analysis and Risk Assessment (TARA) at component, function and vehicle level

Defining cybersecurity goals, concepts and requirements together with architects and system designers

Securing software-defined vehicle architectures: central compute, zonal architectures and vehicle-to-cloud connectivity

Secure boot, secure software updates and OTA, key management and PKI

Supporting compliance with ISO/SAE 21434, UNECE R155/R156 and type approval

Supplier cybersecurity reviews and work product assessments

Vulnerability management and post-production cybersecurity monitoring

What we’re looking for

Experience in automotive or embedded cybersecurity

Hands-on experience with TARA and ISO/SAE 21434

Good understanding of UNECE R155/R156 and CSMS

Ability to work with architects, developers, suppliers and other stakeholders

Fluent English. Swedish is a plus.

It’s a plus if you have experience with

Software-defined vehicles: service-oriented architectures (SOA), AUTOSAR Adaptive, high-performance computers (HPC) and zonal architectures

Connected vehicles: OTA/SUMS, vehicle-to-cloud security, V2X and telematics

Embedded security: HSM, secure boot, SecOC, secure diagnostics (UDS 0x27/0x29) and cryptography

Platforms: AUTOSAR Classic, Linux/QNX and Android Automotive

Networks: CAN/CAN FD, automotive Ethernet, MACsec and IDS/IDPS

Secure development: secure software development, DevSecOps, SBOM and supply-chain security

Testing: security testing and penetration testing of ECUs and vehicle systems

Related standards: ISO 26262 (functional safety), ISO/SAE 21434 with China GB 44495, and the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA)

What we offer

Assignments with leading automotive companies in the Gothenburg region

The choice of employment at Cyber Instincts or working with us as an independent subconsultant

A small, specialised cybersecurity company with short decision paths and close contact with management

Location: Gothenburg. The setup is hybrid or on-site depending on the assignment.
We review applications continuously, and you are welcome to apply even if we have no matching assignment right now.
